clue.text: Sticky stuff, porridge served with fruit

parts.note: porridge is British slang for time in prison, as is bird (from rhyming slang bird-lime = time)
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A breakfast of porridge topped with fruit, which turns out to be sticky.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge and bird are both British slang for a prison sentence; the sticky stuff is apt, since bird-lime is the source of the rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdlime is a glue smeared on twigs to trap small birds, a classic sticky substance.

clue.text: Bully Bishop defeated after argument

indicators.note: the word for defeated comes after the word for argument

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or argument
to beat is to defeat; beat here is the past participle

explanation.surface: A bishop who lost an argument turned to bullying.
explanation.definitionFit: To browbeat is to intimidate with stern words, a verb synonym of bully.

clue.text: Public stage with section covered by garbage and booze

indicators.note: the letter for section is enclosed by the word for garbage

parts.note: rot means nonsense or garbage
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A public platform partly strewn with rubbish and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform from which a speaker addresses an audience.

clue.text: Choice of sides with variable vehicle

parts.note: a choice between the two sides is left or right, L or R
x, y and z are the usual algebraic variables

explanation.surface: A vehicle that can be driven from either side.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorry is the British term for a truck, a large goods vehicle.

clue.text: Spooner's cake mix instruction, as it happens, including a bit of extravagant fantasy

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the instruction is said with its first consonants exchanged

parts.note: a cake mix's instruction is 'bake me', like Alice's 'Eat me' labels

indicators.note: the word for happening now takes the letter inside it

parts.note: a live broadcast goes out as it happens

indicators.note: a bit of the word means just its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of extravagant

explanation.surface: A cake-mix packet's instructions, as written, hint at a little extravagant fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The instruction is 'bake me', like Alice's 'Eat me' labels; Spooner turns it into MAKE BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-believe is pretending or imaginative play, a noun synonym of fantasy.

clue.text: Jeers "Third rate, and not working on board"

indicators.note: 'on board' means aboard a vessel, so the other letters are placed within the ship

parts.note: board evokes the ship one is aboard, and SS is the abbreviation for steamship
C is the third grade, after A and B
a machine that is off is not working

explanation.surface: Mockery of a third-rate crew member who does nothing on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the crossword convention for going inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to mock or ridicule, so scoffs and jeers are verb synonyms.

clue.text: A standard set in reconstruction of larch thicket

indicators.note: the letters for 'a standard' are placed inside the rearranged tree
reconstruction means rebuilding, so the tree's letters are reordered

parts.note: par is the standard score or level

explanation.surface: A standard is erected while rebuilding a thicket of larch.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaparral is the dense scrub of the American Southwest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaparral is dense, tangled evergreen scrubland, so it is a kind of thicket.

clue.text: Hide mistake in polish

parts.note: an animal's hide is its fur or pelt
bish is old British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: Covering up an error while doing some polishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hide looks like a verb meaning conceal; here it is an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To furbish is to burnish or brighten up, a verb synonym of polish.

clue.text: Easier wiping lecturer's silly smile

indicators.note: wiping means erasing, so the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: simpler means easier
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: Things got easier once someone wiped the lecturer's silly grin away.
explanation.definitionFit: A simper is an affected, coy or foolish smile.

clue.text: Not at work, expecting to receive delivery

definitions.meaning: first meaning: taking industrial action, refusing to work
second meaning: in cricket, the batsman ... is the one facing the next ball bowled

explanation.walkthrough: A delivery in cricket is a ball bowled; the batter who will face it is said to be on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who have walked out in a dispute are described as being out of work by choice, i.e. withdrawing labour.

clue.text: Aromatic liquid from a yard In Birmingham

indicators.note: the letters for 'a yard' are placed inside the word for Birmingham

parts.note: Brum is the informal name for the English city of Birmingham

explanation.surface: Some fragrant liquid obtained from a yard in Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay rum is a scented lotion distilled from bay leaves and rum, used as an aftershave or hair tonic.

clue.text: Well-built railway linked to British Unionist

explanation.surface: A sturdy railway line connected to a British Unionist politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Burly describes someone large and strongly built, a synonym of well-built.

clue.text: Sex and more sex grabbed by feeble person with delusions

parts.note: to bed someone is to have sex with them

indicators.note: the word for 'more sex' is held inside the word for feeble

parts.note: a lame excuse is a feeble one
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A weak person obsessed with sex is surely deluded.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedlam was the old London asylum, Bethlem Hospital, so its inmates were Bedlamites.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bedlamite is a lunatic, someone deranged and prone to delusions, after the famous asylum.

clue.text: Worker unexpectedly ready to embrace political party

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the party inside them
something done unexpectedly is out of its expected order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: Labour is a British political party

explanation.surface: A worker who unexpectedly turned out willing to back a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A day labourer is a casual worker hired and paid one day at a time.

clue.text: Matriarch, lady wangling prominent place in London

indicators.note: wangling means manipulating or fiddling, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A grand old lady scheming her way into a prestigious London address.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiralty Arch is the ceremonial gateway between Trafalgar Square and The Mall in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch is a landmark building at a conspicuous spot near Trafalgar Square in central London.

clue.text: Biblical passage about religious education giving new interpretation

indicators.note: about means around, so the passage goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a reading is a passage of scripture read aloud in church

explanation.surface: A lesson from Scripture in RE class offering a fresh take.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school subject Religious Education.
explanation.definitionFit: A rereading of a text is a fresh reading of it, offering a revised understanding.

clue.text: Snake holed up in plant of death

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: up here means disturbed or in disorder, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A snake lurking in a deadly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holed up' looks like hiding; 'up' is the anagram signal on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel was linked in Greek myth with the dead, covering the meadows of the underworld.

clue.text: Parts of the brain exercised by Opera Bastille?

indicators.note: exercised suggests being worked over or moved about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Which parts of your brain get a workout at the Paris opera house?
explanation.walkthrough: The Opéra Bastille is the modern Paris opera house; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The parietal lobes are two regions of the cerebral cortex handling sensory information, near the crown of the head.

clue.text: Test eliminating E. coli regularly brought up about second condition

indicators.note: eliminating means removing, so the letter is taken out

parts.note: to prove something is to test it, as in the proof of the pudding

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed letters go round the abbreviation
in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top
regularly means taking every other letter

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of coli

explanation.surface: A lab test that eliminated E. coli, reported with a second condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E. coli' looks like one name, but the E is removed from the test and only 'coli' is the source of the alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a stipulation or clause attached to an agreement, i.e. a condition.

clue.text: Man, in short, tucking into fish or other living material

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the fish

parts.note: the bass is a fish
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man eating fish or some other organic food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Biomass is the total mass of organisms in an area, or organic matter used as fuel.

clue.text: Numerical data about university ranking

indicators.note: about means around, so the data word surrounds the letter

parts.note: stats is short for statistics

explanation.surface: Statistics on a university's place in the league tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or position in a hierarchy, a synonym of ranking.

clue.text: Decorator transformed Parisian location

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An interior designer gave a makeover to a spot in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trocadéro is a district of Paris across the Seine from the Eiffel Tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trocadéro is a well-known Parisian area and square, home to the Palais de Chaillot.

clue.text: Reluctant to follow Catholic clergy

indicators.note: the word for reluctant comes after the abbreviation for Catholic

parts.note: loth (or loath) means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to go along with the Catholic priesthood.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The cloth' is an idiom for the clergy, from the clerical clothing they wear.

clue.text: Policeman sent up to secure border bend

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the reversed letters hold the border inside
in a down clue, sent up means written from bottom to top

parts.note: PC is a police constable
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A police officer posted to guard a bend near the border.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp is to press into small folds or waves, so it is to bend or crease.

clue.text: Case finishing early, having involved one with very minor matters

indicators.note: the shortened word for case takes the other letters inside it
finishing early means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a legal case is a trial
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A court case that ended early after being caught up in very minor matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivia are trifles, details of little importance, so the plural noun fits minor matters.

clue.text: God enthralling Rector and would-be minister

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the god's name holds the letter inside it

parts.note: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology

explanation.surface: A pagan god captivating a rector and an aspiring priest.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinand is a candidate preparing for ordination into the ministry of a church.

clue.text: Small, smelly and squishy

parts.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell, so pongy means smelly

explanation.surface: A list of three adjectives for something small, smelly and soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spongy is soft and compressible, yielding like a sponge when squeezed.

clue.text: Offer page with correction to 'parosol'

indicators.note: the misspelled word is corrected by putting its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A proposal to fix a page where 'parasol' has been misspelt.
explanation.walkthrough: The misspelling 'parosol' is deliberate; correcting it to parasol would be the false path, but its letters are simply rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is something put forward for acceptance, a noun synonym of an offer.
